places.name: Troy
places.note: The city the Achaeans sacked after ten years of war; its ruins are at Hisarlik in north-west Turkey.

places.name: Ithaca
places.note: Ulysses' rocky home island in the Ionian Sea, traditionally the modern island of Ithaki.

places.name: Neritum
places.note: The wooded mountain of Ithaca, traditionally Mount Niritos in the north of the island.

places.name: Ogygian island
places.note: Calypso's island, far out in the sea. Since antiquity often identified with Gozo, off Malta.

places.name: Pylos
places.note: Nestor's sandy Pylos on the western Peloponnese; pinned at the Mycenaean 'Palace of Nestor'.

places.name: Sparta
places.note: Menelaus' city in the valley of Lacedaemon, in the southern Peloponnese.

places.name: Scheria
places.note: Land of the seafaring Phaeacians, traditionally Corfu (Butler himself argued for Trapani in Sicily).

places.name: Ismarus
places.note: City of the Cicons on the Thracian coast, near modern Maroneia.

places.name: Cape Malea
places.note: The stormy south-eastern cape of the Peloponnese, where ships are blown off course.

places.name: Cythera
places.note: Island off Cape Malea, modern Kythira.

places.name: land of the Lotus-eaters
places.note: Land of those who eat the lotus; ancient tradition places it on Djerba, off Tunisia.

places.name: land of the Cyclopes
places.note: Country of the one-eyed giants, traditionally the coast below Etna in Sicily (the Cyclops rocks at Aci Trezza).

places.name: Aeolian island
places.note: Home of Aeolus, keeper of the winds, traditionally Lipari north of Sicily.

places.name: Laestrygonians
places.note: The rocky stronghold of Lamus-Telepylus; ancient writers placed it at Formiae (Formia) on the coast of Latium.

places.name: Aeaean island
places.note: Circe's island, traditionally the promontory of Monte Circeo, south of Rome.

places.name: island of the two Sirens
places.note: Where the Sirens sing; traditionally the Li Galli islets off the Amalfi coast.

places.name: Scylla
places.note: A monster's cave on one side of a narrow strait, traditionally Scilla on the Calabrian side of the Strait of Messina.

places.name: Charybdis
places.note: The whirlpool across the strait from Scylla, traditionally off Capo Peloro, Sicily.

places.name: Thrinacian island
places.note: Island of the sun-god's herds, traditionally Sicily; ancient writers put the herds near Mylae (Milazzo).

places.name: Crete
places.note: The great island south of the Aegean, home of Idomeneus and once of Minos.

places.name: Egypt
places.note: The land of the Nile (Homer's river Aegyptus); pinned in the Delta, where Greek ships put in.

places.name: Olympus
places.note: The mountain home of the gods, on the border of Thessaly and Macedonia.

places.name: Argos
places.note: City and plain in the north-east Peloponnese.

places.name: Dulichium
places.note: A wheat-growing island near Ithaca whose site is disputed; often placed at Lefkada.

places.name: Zacynthus
places.note: The wooded island south of Ithaca, modern Zakynthos.

places.name: Tenedos
places.note: Small island off the coast of Troy, modern Bozcaada.

places.name: Lesbos
places.note: The large island off the coast of Asia Minor, south of Troy.

places.name: Chios
places.note: Island on the sea route home from Troy, south of Lesbos.

places.name: Euboea
places.note: The long island lying along the coast of mainland Greece.

places.name: Athens
places.note: City of Erechtheus, dear to Minerva.

places.name: Cyprus
places.note: Island of the eastern Mediterranean, sacred to Venus.

places.name: Phoenicia
places.note: The coast of the seafaring Phoenicians, pinned at Sidon.

places.name: Libya
places.note: Homer's Libya: the coast west of Egypt, pinned near Benghazi.

places.name: Thesprotian coast
places.note: The coast of the Thesprotians in Epirus, on the mainland north of Ithaca.

places.name: Dodona
places.note: Jove's oracle of the oak in Epirus.

places.name: Parnassus
places.note: The mountain above Delphi, where Autolycus and his sons hunt.

places.name: Elis
places.note: Land of the Epeans on the north-west Peloponnese, over against Ithaca.

places.name: Hellespont
places.note: The strait by Troy, today's Dardanelles.
